'''Vijay Kumar Patodi''' (12 March 1945 – 21 December 1976) was an Indian [[mathematician]] who made fundamental contributions to [[differential geometry]] and [[topology]].  He was the first mathematician to apply [[heat equation]] methods to the proof of the [[Atiyah–Singer index theorem|index theorem]] for elliptic operators.{{citation needed|date=March 2011}} He was a [[professor]] at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], [[Mumbai (Bombay)]].

==Education==
Patodi was a graduate of Government High School, [[Guna, India|Guna]], [[Madhya Pradesh]].  He received his bachelor's degree from Vikram University, [[Ujjain]], his master's degree from the [[Benaras Hindu University]], and his Ph.D. from the [[University of Bombay]] under the guidance of M. S. Narasimhan and S. Ramanan at the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]].<ref>{{Cite book
| url = https://books.google.com/books?id=TXje34eAhhEC
| title = Concise Biography
| isbn = 9789810246266
| last1 = Pathak
| first1 = R. S.
| year = 2001
| publisher = World Scientific
}}</ref>

In the two papers based on his Ph.D. thesis, "Curvature and Eigenforms of the Laplace Operator" (''Journal of Differential Geometry''), and "An Analytical Proof of the Riemann-Roch-Hirzebruch Formula for Kaehler Manifolds" (also ''Journal of Differential Geometry''), Patodi made his fundamental breakthroughs.<ref>{{Cite web
| url = http://vijay.com/other-vijays/vijay-patodi/
| title = Biography
| access-date = 20 October 2015
| archive-date = 7 August 2018
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180807161949/http://vijay.com/other-vijays/vijay-patodi/
| url-status = dead
}}</ref>

==Research career==
He was invited to spend 1971–1973 at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]], [[New Jersey]], where he collaborated with [[Michael Atiyah]], [[Isadore Singer]], and [[Raoul Bott]].  The joint work led to a series of papers, "Spectral Asymmetry and Riemannian Geometry" with Atiyah and Singer,<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Atiyah | first1=M. F. | authorlink1=Michael Atiyah
| last2=Patodi | first2=V. K.
| last3=Singer | first3=I. M. | authorlink3=Isadore Singer
| title=Spectral asymmetry and Riemannian Geometry I
| journal=[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]
| volume=77
| issue=1
| date=1975
| pages=43–69
| doi=10.1017/S0305004100049410| bibcode=1975MPCPS..77...43A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Atiyah | first1=M. F. | authorlink1=Michael Atiyah
| last2=Patodi | first2=V. K.
| last3=Singer | first3=I. M. | authorlink3=Isadore Singer
| title=Spectral asymmetry and Riemannian Geometry II
| journal=[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]
| volume=78
| issue=3
| date=1975
| pages=405–432
| doi=10.1017/S0305004100051872| bibcode=1975MPCPS..78..405A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Atiyah | first1=M. F. | authorlink1=Michael Atiyah
| last2=Patodi | first2=V. K.
| last3=Singer | first3=I. M. | authorlink3=Isadore Singer
| title=Spectral asymmetry and Riemannian Geometry III
| journal=[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]
| volume=79
| issue=1
| date=1976
| pages=71–99
| doi=10.1017/S0305004100052105| bibcode=1976MPCPS..79...71A }}</ref> in which the [[η-invariant]] was defined.  This invariant was to play a major role in subsequent advances in the area in the 1980s.<ref>{{Cite web
| url = http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Patodi.html
| title = Biography
}}</ref>

Patodi was promoted to full professor at Tata Institute at age 30, however, he died at age 31, as a result of complications prior to surgery for a kidney transplant.
